reason: The cited evidence does not directly support Hf-induced precipitation strengthening in TiVNbTa at 1273 K. E3 shows precipitation kinetics in a different FCC HEA, E4 shows oxide-induced precipitation in a different RHEA, and E5 discusses Laves phase suppression in HfMoNbTaW, none of which establish the claimed mechanism or performance for the proposed alloy. The key premises thus lack specific prior evidence.
premises: Hf addition to TiVNbTa can form coherent Hf-rich nano-precipitates via aging
Such precipitates will hinder dislocation motion at 1273 K, raising yield strength above 500 MPa
The precipitates will not severely degrade ductility (strain remains ~30% or above)
The precipitates will not degrade thermal conductivity below the required level for W-to-CuCrZr heat transfer
The aging treatment can be optimized to avoid deleterious coarsening or inhomogeneity
